newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico truckers present demands to Senate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico truckers present demands to Senate.

text.p: Mexican legislators on Thursday warmly received leaders of a pro-government truckers group and said the Senate would consider a list of their demands.
At the same time, the lawmakers slammed an independent group that is staging a strike to achieve similar goals.

"Waiving road tax and Trade Ministry registration fees, lower highway tolls and greater highway security," were the demands listed in a statement by the Mexican National Truckers' Confederation (Canatram).
The president of the Senate Transportation Committee, Francisco Davila, said he would call for a Senate meeting to review the demands.
Davila also praised the Canatram for not joining a strike by members of the independent National "Adolfo Lopez Mateos" Transport Drivers Confederation. The job action began on Monday.
The senator branded the strike as being the work of "movements of shady little groups that do not represent the majority interests of the transportation sector."
The independent truckers claim a membership of 40,000, while the Canatram claims 100,000.
Until January 1, formally registered Mexican businesses were required by law to affiliate with a relevant industry chamber, which must in turn become affiliated with a nationwide confederation.
Many business owners complained the chambers were bureaucratic, inefficient organizations that toed the government line and did little in exchange for members' fees.
